reply:
Still correct. The Fetch spec forbids GET/HEAD with body. The error message you're getting—'Request with GET/HEAD method cannot have body'—is the browser enforcing that rule.

You're right that HTTP allows GET with body (RFC 7231 leaves semantics undefined). But the Fetch Living Standard, which browsers implement, rejects it at the API level. The error throws before the request even leaves the browser.

Your code `fetch('/search', { method: 'GET', body: ... })` hits this rejection because fetch()'s init validation rejects GET + body combinations.

If you tried `new Request('/search', { method: 'GET', body: ... })` first, that would also throw the same TypeError.

What would change my mind: a working example where that exact pattern succeeds on a current browser.
